[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda - status on creds, staging activation, run a smoke bench, and any security blockers. Priya are you good to start?
[00:18] Priya (CTO): Yeah thanks Maya. Jordan's going to walk through where we are with the VPC stuff, but high level we want staging activated by Friday and a short bench to validate 100 qps at 128 token average, p95 under 300 ms ideally. That is sorta the bar to determine whether we move to dedicated later.
[00:36] Jordan (Platform Eng): Right, so we spun up the staging subnets, there was an issue with an allowlist on our side - the firewall only allowed outbound 443 to specific IPs. I removed that but need the exact egress IPs for Redwood to ensure NAT rule mapping.
[00:52] Maya (AE): Cool, we'll send the egress IP list. Daniel, do we have an ephemeral creds option we can hand off so Jordan can kick the bench without long-lived keys?
[01:05] Daniel (SE): Yeah we can provide short-lived tokens via the console or generate service account keys scoped to just inference. Note, if you want VPC peering for Private deploy we'll need the CIDR ranges and a test VLAN. Also small gotcha: if you route through a corporate proxy it may break our gRPC streaming and that'll inflate tail latency.
[01:28] Alex (SRE): We are behind a proxy, yes — corporate proxy with TLS-inspection. Could that be the issue?
[01:33] Daniel (SE): Possibly. TLS re-write can interfere. For streaming we recommend either bypassing TLS-inspection for the Redwood endpoints or use a NATed subnet that doesn't go through the proxy.
[01:45] Priya (CTO): Okay we'll try the bypass for the staging run. Samir, from security side any blockers on short-lived tokens?
[01:52] Samir (Security): Short-lived tokens are fine. The bigger asks are KMS integration and ensuring logs are retained in our SIEM. We need to see where audit logs live — are they pushed to our Splunk or do we pull them? Also send any SOC2 artifacts.
[02:07] Maya (AE): We can push audit logs to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules or set up forwarding into Splunk, whichever you prefer. We'll attach our SOC2 certs and an HSM/KMS integration note after the call.
[02:20] Priya (CTO): Great. On latency: Daniel, can you summarize expected p95/p99 on a m60-like host? There's some variance in our workload because we have a lot of short prompts.
[02:29] Daniel (SE): Sure. For short prompts (avg 80-150 tokens) on a single A100-ish or M60-equivalent instance you'll see p95 ~120-220ms depending on batching. But if a proxy introduces extra RTTs or if you enable prefix caching you'll see different curves. Also quantization and QKV optimizations matter — for some of our curated models the KV cache handling can be the largest swing.
[02:55] Jordan (Platform Eng): You mentioned KV cache — Daniel said K V cash last week and we were like what?
[03:00] (laughter)
[03:03] Daniel (SE): My accent turned it into K V cash, yeah.
[03:07] Maya (AE): Real world transcript right there.
[03:10] Olivia (SE): Quick note: if you expect burst traffic, Redwood Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserve slots. Otherwise hosted will autoscale but might be less predictable for bursty traffic.
[03:22] Priya (CTO): We're leaning hosted for the pilot but want to validate numbers first. Ideally we avoid provisioning dedicated until we prove cost per token is favorable.
[03:34] Samir (Security): Also we need to confirm data residency for logs — our legal team wants retention controls and encryption keys under our KMS. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[03:44] Daniel (SE): Yes, support for CMK via standard KMS integrations. There are two deployment shapes: for Redwood Private we can bring-your-own-KMS; for hosted we provide envelope encryption with optional customer-managed keys in some tiers. We'll add exact config docs.
[03:58] Jordan (Platform Eng): For the bench, we will create traffic that approximates our peak — 120 qps ramp to 300 qps for 10 minutes then steady. Do you want a focused p95/p99 report only or full token breakdown?
[04:12] Daniel (SE): Full is best: p50/p95/p99, cpu/gpu utilization, token counts, and any dropped requests. If you can include sample prompt shapes that hit our system that helps correlate.
[04:24] Alex (SRE): We can provide sample prompt templates; note some have function calling payloads which increase length, may skew latency a bit.
[04:32] Priya (CTO): Good call. Maya, what's the SOW timeline if we move to a short pilot?
[04:37] Maya (AE): We'll send a pilot SOW draft today — 4-week pilot, staging access, up to X compute hours (we'll define), and pricing bands. If the bench looks good we'll propose dedicated trial options.
[04:48] Samir (Security): Also need to review your pen test cycle and incident response. Do you do monthly scans?
[04:55] Daniel (SE): We run quarterly pentests and can share redacted reports. We also have SOC2 Type II. We'll include incident response summary in the security pack.
[05:06] Priya (CTO): Perfect. Anything else on the infra side?
[05:11] Jordan (Platform Eng): One more — Network MTU mismatch previously caused fragmented packets; our infra team flagged a 1400 MTU in our colo. If your service expects 1500 we should be aware.
[05:22] Daniel (SE): Good catch. We'll run a check for fragmentation and recommend adjustments if we see high retransmits.
[05:29] Maya (AE): ok let's recap owners and dates quickly. Daniel will run the initial bench and send results; Jordan will provide creds and traffic shapes; Maya will send SOW and runbook; Samir will confirm KMS/retention asks.
[05:41] Priya (CTO): Sounds good. Also if the bench fails due to the proxy we may need a separate network call; please be ready to triage.
[05:49] Daniel (SE): Yep. If we see drops we'll setup packet captures and a network deep-dive.
[05:55] Jordan (Platform Eng): We'll aim to have the creds in by tomorrow morning.
[06:00] Maya (AE): Fantastic. Any last questions?
[06:03] Alex (SRE): Quick question about logs — is there an endpoint to stream and subscribe to inference traces or do you only export batches?
[06:12] Daniel (SE): There's both: you can stream sample inference traces for debugging during the bench and we can also dump aggregated logs to S3 or forward to Splunk. Streaming may be noisy so we usually do a sampled stream.
[06:26] Priya (CTO): OK thanks everyone. We'll circulate the remaining details in JIRA when Jordan posts creds.
[06:32] Maya (AE): Great — we'll share runbook and SOC2 docs by EOD. Talk soon.

End of transcript.
